page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a narrow dark strip at the right edge (the neighbouring page). A printed page number and running head sit at the top. One small dash stands in the left margin beside the line "mitteret". No notes, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.l: catrici, ideoque tam Deus ab intrinseca bonita-
te punit, quam benefacit. Hoc non possunt
negare Arminiani, nisi velint Deum non esse tam
essentialiter iustum, quam bonum, quod est
absurdum: nulla enim attributa essentialia infunt
Deo per magis, aut minus, imo neque
creaturæ. Homo enim tam essentialiter est
animal, quam est rationalis, quamvis Deus
non essentialiter benefaciat ulli creaturæ: sic
enim necessitate naturæ, creaturam, *cui be-
nefaceret, condidisse oportuit: quod dogma
non est Christianum, sed potius Aristoteli-
cum. Ideoque necesse est, Deus antecedente
voluntate velit omnes homines peccatores pe-
rire, ideoque non potuit Christum redemp-
tionem humani generis in mundum mittere.
Arminiani enim docent omnes homines esse
peccatores antecedenter ad missionem, imo
ad decretum mittendi Christum. Rationem
jam quæro ex Arminianis, cur Deus ex naturali
voluntate salvandi homines, qua creaturas,
mitteret salvatorem, euangelium indulgeret,
vocaret omnes, promissis & poenis propositis
&c. & non pari ratione ex naturali Dei volun-
tate perdendi omnes homines qua peccatores,
negaret omnibus Christum redemptorem,
euangelium, & vocationem, tum commu-
nem, tum specialem, & gratiam sufficien-
tem, omniaque salutis media. Sed ego
vereor ne negent voluntatem naturalem per-
dendi peccatores, quam Grevinchovius ipso-
rum doctrinæ convenienter admodum & occu-

page.notes: Running head and page number are read from a small, worn print at the top; "Antecedente" and the page number are doubtful. The first word "catrici" begins a line and is the end of a word from the previous page ("Creatrici"). The "*" before "cui" is probably a printed reference mark or a speck; it is kept as printed. The dash in the left margin beside "mitteret" looks like a printer's line marker, not a note, so it is left out. The text ends with "occu-" hyphenated at the line end; the word continues on the next page. Printed "iuftum" and "intrinfeca" were read as "iustum" and "intrinseca" (long s as s).
